quotations.exact_text_latex:
(i) If we restrict functions on $Z(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$, $U_Z(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ to $U_Y(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ via $\phi$, then
\[
\mathrm{log\text{-}cond}_E-\mathrm{log\text{-}cond}_D\lesssim\mathrm{log\text{-}diff}_Y-\mathrm{log\text{-}diff}_Z\lesssim\left(1-\frac{1}{e}\right)\cdot\mathrm{log\text{-}cond}_E
\]
on $U_Y(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$.
quotations.context_not_quote: Here φ:Y→Z is a generically finite morphism of normal Z-proper Z-flat dimension-two schemes; D and E are effective Z-flat Cartier divisors with reduced generic fibers, D_Q=φ_Q^{-1}(E_Q)_red, finite étale restriction off the divisors, and ramification indices along D_Q dividing e. The statement uses BD-class comparisons (≲), not an exact numerical finite-set inequality.

quotations.exact_text_latex: Fix a prime number $p$ and a positive integer $d$. Then there exists a positive integer $n$ such that for any finite Galois extension $L/K$ of finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ with $[L:K]\leq d$, the different ideal of $L/K$ contains $p^n\cdot\mathcal{O}_L$ [where we write $\mathcal{O}_L$ for the ring of integers of $L$].
quotations.context_not_quote: The preceding proof paragraph reduces boundedness of the portion over a finite set Σ of log-diff_Y−log-diff_Z to this elementary local claim. This is supporting background, not the exact new finite-set conductor-extension child.
